last_report.behaviour_change:
Neither GS200 can now have its output switched on, or its function changed, in a way that applies an unramped voltage or current step.

Charge line (build_context/connect calls the new open_charge_yoko):
- Before opening anything, it refuses the TWPA source. Addresses are compared by GPIB (board, primary address), so GPIB1::12, GPIB1::12::INSTR, gpib1::12::0::INSTR and other spellings of the shared constant hardware.yoko.TWPA_YOKO_ADDRESS (GPIB1::12::INSTR) are all refused. A VISA alias is not resolved.
- It then queries :OUTP?, :SOUR:FUNC? and :SOUR:LEV? and prints the results.
- CURR with the output ON: it raises without writing anything and closes the session.
- Output OFF: it writes :SOUR:FUNC VOLT, reads :SOUR:RANG?, writes :SOUR:LEV 0, and only then writes :OUTP ON. A stale stored setpoint is never applied, and ramp_to ramps from 0.
- Output already ON in VOLT: the level is left alone, and ramp_to ramps from the real level.
- In both cases it raises before the output goes on if the active range is above 10 V or if |start_voltage| > 1.2x the range. The range above 10 V is the 30 V range: it resolves only 1 mV, coarser than the readback tolerance, and the charge line never needs it.
- It never changes the range.

ramp_to:
- Rejects |target| > 10 V on both signs with ValueError "|target| = X V exceeds the 10 V charge-line limit". Before, -50 V passed.
- After landing, it reads back :SOUR:LEV? and raises RuntimeError if the level is more than 1e-4 V away. The message names both possible causes: clipped by the range, or rounded by a coarse range.
- Its signature and its ramp write sequence are unchanged.

TWPA (set_bias.main and flux_sweep.main call the new enable_current_output_safely(yoko, range_A)):
- It queries and prints :OUTP?, :SOUR:FUNC? and :SOUR:LEV?.
- Output OFF: it writes FUNC CURR, RANG, LEV 0, then OUTP ON. The ramp starts at 0 A instead of jumping to a stale setpoint at about 1e4 uA/s.
- ON in VOLT: it raises.
- ON in CURR: it keeps the setpoint and changes the range only at 0 A. At a nonzero level it keeps a larger active range and raises on a smaller one. It returns the active range, and flux_sweep records that range.
- flux_sweep's finally block ramps to 0 only if the enable step succeeded.

Programs, cfg and payloads are unchanged.
tests_added: tests/test_yoko_safety.py: 26 tests with a scripted fake GS200.
TWPA, output OFF: writes exactly FUNC CURR, RANG 0.001, LEV 0, OUTP ON.
TWPA, ON+VOLT: refused with no writes.
TWPA, ON+CURR: keeps the setpoint. The range is changed only at 0 A, and a smaller range at a nonzero level raises.
ramp_current after enable starts at 0 and stays within the rate cap.
Charge, OFF: FUNC VOLT, then RANG?, then LEV 0, then OUTP ON.
Charge, ON+VOLT: leaves the level alone.
Charge, ON+CURR: refused with no writes, and the session is closed.
The TWPA address is refused before opening, in 5 spellings, with the fake source parked OFF in CURR. Other GPIB addresses are accepted (GPIB1::9, GPIB0::12, GPIB1::120).
The 30 V range is refused before LEV 0 and OUTP ON, with the output off and with it on. The 10 V range is accepted.
A start voltage above 1.2x the range is refused.

ramp_to rejects 10.5, -10.5 and -50 V with no traffic. New this round: the test also matches the exact message text 'exceeds the 10 V charge-line limit' that docs/troubleshooting.md quotes, so the two cannot drift apart again.
ramp_to ends with the landing write plus a LEV? readback, and a readback mismatch raises.

(2) On the TWPA side, with the output ON in CURR at a nonzero level, an active range smaller than range_A raises even when the target would fit in the active range, for example when YOKO_CURR_RANGE_A is forced larger than needed.
findings.evidence: In open_charge_yoko: `if v_range > CHARGE_V_LIMIT: raise ValueError(...)`. This is justified: the 1 mV resolution on that range would trip the 1e-4 V readback on 0.5 mV sweet-spot steps. In enable_current_output_safely the final `raise RuntimeError(...)` applies whenever active < range_A and stored != 0. Both cases fail safe (no write) and both are documented in hardware.md and troubleshooting.md.

last_review.summary: The F21 fix is correct, and it is complete across all yoko call sites: every charge-line open goes through build_context -> open_charge_yoko, and both TWPA scripts use enable_current_output_safely. I re-derived the golden impact over all 40 labels, all 40 on board A and 6 spot-checked on B. Once the old bring-up is replaced with the new 7-entry block and the per-ramp_to LEV? readbacks are removed, every new yoko_writes sequence equals the golden, so the yoko traffic changes exactly as intended and in nothing else. The other field-class diffs that show up (T1/T2E fits, spectroscopy, zero-span validation) come from other agents' concurrent edits and must be kept out of the F21 golden. There are no must-fix items. Two should-fix items concern the orchestrator's commit and golden handling, not the code. (1) The F21 hunks in charge_sweep.md and charge_transmission_sweep.md were already committed in F28's c46424ce, so there is nothing to stage there, and HEAD's docs currently describe F21 behaviour. (2) The golden impact covers all 40 labels on both boards, including RunChargeSweep[yoko_fixed] (7->13), not only the 3 labels the implementer ran. The notes cover: a missing within-tolerance readback test, the conservative 30 V and TWPA range refusals, a cosmetic error-message claim, and an unrelated tests/refactor failure from zero_span_validation.
